lessons.title: Connect your account
lessons.goal: One secure sign-in. A workspace for your devices.
lessons.intro: Let’s get you connected. Your fleet is the workspace where you’ll organize devices and manage their updates.
lessons.outro: You’re signed in and your fleet is selected. Next, let’s check how many devices you can manage.

actions.label: Start in the console
actions.text: Open Get started. This gives you a clear view of what to do next.

actions.label: Choose how to sign in
actions.text: Choose your wallet, or another sign-in method offered by your console.

actions.label: Approve the connection
actions.text: This walkthrough uses a demo account. Approve the connection in your own wallet; your private key stays there.

actions.label: Check your account
actions.text: Check that the console shows the account you intended to connect.

actions.label: Create your first fleet
actions.text: On your first visit, create your default fleet and approve the request.

actions.label: Choose your workspace
actions.text: Select your fleet. You can now manage its devices from this workspace.

lessons.recap: Your fleet is selected. Check capacity before adding devices.

lessons.title: Choose your device capacity
lessons.goal: Know how many devices your plan can include.
lessons.intro: Before adding devices, check your capacity. Your subscription sets the device limit; operating funds are managed separately.
lessons.outro: Capacity is active in this example. Next, add the operating funds your devices will use.

actions.label: Check the device limit
actions.text: Open Device capacity and check how many devices your organization can manage.

actions.label: Review the plan
actions.text: This demonstration uses a test plan. Review the device allowance and price shown in your own console.

actions.label: Review before approving
actions.text: Check the amount and recipient before approving prepayment. This is separate from device operating funds.

actions.label: Activate the capacity
actions.text: Apply the payment when it is due. Check the wallet request before approving; a network fee may still apply.

actions.label: Confirm the allowance
actions.text: Check the updated device allowance. Adding operating funds later will not change this limit.

lessons.recap: Operating funds are separate from your device allowance.

lessons.title: Fund device activity
lessons.goal: Keep operating funds separate from device capacity.
lessons.intro: Your devices need operating funds to send reports and carry out network activity. Let’s add those funds to your fleet.
lessons.outro: The deposit is confirmed. Device health is checked separately. Next, register your first device.

actions.label: Open Network budget
actions.text: Choose Network budget. This balance covers device activity, rather than your subscription allowance.

actions.label: Choose an amount
actions.text: Enter the amount to add. File and log storage have separate funding controls.

actions.label: Approve the deposit
actions.text: Review the deposit in your wallet, then approve it.

actions.label: Check the balance
actions.text: Look for the confirmed deposit under Keep devices reporting. Funding alone does not mean a device is online.

lessons.recap: A funded budget is separate from device readiness and health.

lessons.title: Register your first device
lessons.goal: Connect a device’s identity to a name you recognize.
lessons.intro: Registration connects a device to your fleet, so updates and reports belong to the right machine. Let’s start with one device.
lessons.outro: Your device is registered. Start its configured client and check for a report before treating it as online.

actions.label: Open Devices
actions.text: Choose Devices. For a small pilot, register the identity created by the installed device client.

actions.label: Use the public identity
actions.text: Choose Register by address. Copy the public identity from device setup; keep its private key on the device.

actions.label: Approve registration
actions.text: Register the device and approve the request in your wallet.

actions.label: Check the device entry
actions.text: The new device appears in your fleet. Registration and online status are different: the client still needs to report.

lessons.recap: Start the configured client and wait for its report.

lessons.title: Prepare a batch of devices
lessons.goal: Set up many devices without registering them one by one.
lessons.intro: For larger fleets, prepare devices in a batch. Each device receives its own single-use setup credential before first boot.
lessons.outro: The batch is prepared. Each device still needs its own credential and the configured client to enroll at first boot.

actions.label: Open Enrollment
actions.text: Choose Enrollment to prepare devices during manufacturing or provisioning.

actions.label: Set the batch limits
actions.text: Set a device limit and expiry before creating a policy. This example reuses an existing policy.

actions.label: Check the device list
actions.text: Paste a roster with names and serial numbers, then check it before continuing.

actions.label: Keep credentials secure
actions.text: Download the credentials and store them securely. This is the only download of these one-use setup keys.

actions.label: Register the reserved devices
actions.text: Register the reserved devices and approve the request. Give each device only its own credential.

actions.label: Wait for first boot
actions.text: The reservations are ready. Devices complete enrollment when their configured clients start with those credentials.

lessons.recap: Keep each device’s credential secure until first boot.

lessons.title: Publish a software release
lessons.goal: Prepare a version once, then deploy it where needed.
lessons.intro: Your software library keeps releases ready for deployment. Let’s publish a version; publishing alone won’t install it on any device.
lessons.outro: Your release is in the library. You’re ready to choose the devices or groups that should receive it.

actions.label: Open Components
actions.text: Choose Components to add a release to your software library.

actions.label: Name the release
actions.text: Name the component and give this release a version number.

actions.label: Add the software
actions.text: Choose the target platform and attach the matching software file.

actions.label: Choose who can read it
actions.text: Use Confidential for proprietary software. This demonstration uses a public file.

actions.label: Upload and approve
actions.text: Review the release, upload it, and approve the request in your wallet. Keep the page open until publication finishes.

actions.label: Check the library
actions.text: Look for the published version in your library. It is available to deploy, but is not installed yet.

lessons.recap: Publishing makes the version available; installation comes later.

lessons.title: Deploy to a device group
lessons.goal: Send one release to the devices that belong together.
lessons.intro: Groups let you update related devices together. We’ll choose a release, send it to a group, and check the device’s result.
lessons.outro: Applied confirms the device completed its installer. Check device health separately before expanding your deployment.

actions.label: Create a device group
actions.text: In Devices, open Device groups. Create a group for the devices you want to manage together.

actions.label: Add the devices
actions.text: Use Manage to add devices. This example reuses a group that is already available.

actions.label: Choose a published version
actions.text: In the library, choose Deploy this version for the release you want to send.

actions.label: Choose the target group
actions.text: Select the group. Desired state keeps this version requested for its members.

actions.label: Approve the deployment
actions.text: Review and approve the deployment. Device clients will process it when they are ready.

actions.label: A request is not a result
actions.text: The deployment is created. That confirms your request, rather than a completed installation.

actions.label: Check device results
actions.text: Open Deployments after the client has processed the update. Check the result reported by the device.

actions.label: Read Applied correctly
actions.text: Applied means the device completed its configured installer. It does not establish that a long-running service is healthy.

lessons.recap: Installation results and current health are separate checks.

lessons.title: Roll out in stages
lessons.goal: Start with a small batch and control what happens next.
lessons.intro: A gradual rollout lets you check a small batch before expanding. We’ll prepare a plan and leave it paused until reporting is ready.
lessons.outro: This plan is saved and paused, with devices still waiting. Check current reporting before approving the next step.

actions.label: Open Rollouts
actions.text: Choose Rollouts to plan a release in stages.

actions.label: Choose the release
actions.text: Create a gradual rollout. Choose the release and the matching device platform.

actions.label: Build your first batch
actions.text: A cohort is simply a batch. Add devices or groups; a device belongs to only one batch.

actions.label: Set the pace
actions.text: Choose the pacing, observation period and failure threshold. Creating the plan does not start devices.

actions.label: Check before admitting devices
actions.text: Select the rollout. Check current device health before allowing the first devices to start.

actions.label: Recognize the waiting state
actions.text: Devices are still waiting in this example. Current reporting must be available before admission.

actions.label: Understand Pause
actions.text: Pause stops new admissions. It does not undo an update already allowed to start; this example admits no devices.

actions.label: Continue when ready
actions.text: The plan is paused. Return when reporting is ready and explicitly approve further progress.

lessons.recap: No devices were admitted in this paused example.

lessons.title: Control private release access
lessons.goal: Choose which devices can open confidential software.
lessons.intro: Private software needs an access policy. This controls who can open encrypted files, without giving them permission to administer your fleet.
lessons.outro: The access rule is saved. Use it when publishing a confidential release, and review membership as your fleet changes.

actions.label: Open Access policies
actions.text: Open Access policies before publishing confidential software. These rules control decryption, not fleet administration.

actions.label: Choose the allowed group
actions.text: Choose Group and select the intended group. Its membership determines which devices may request access keys.

actions.label: Understand revocation
actions.text: The grant is saved. Removing access stops future key requests; it cannot erase files that were already decrypted.

lessons.recap: Removing access cannot recall already decrypted files.

lessons.title: Choose your fleet’s rhythm
lessons.goal: Balance how fresh reports need to be with operating cost.
lessons.intro: Choose how often devices check for updates and send reports. The right cadence depends on your needs and the cost of device activity.
lessons.outro: Your settings are saved for the next device check. Keep the operating budget funded separately as you continue managing the fleet.

actions.label: Choose the reporting cadence
actions.text: Open Fleet settings. Choose update and report intervals; daily reporting is not live monitoring.

actions.label: Review before saving
actions.text: Review the estimate, then save your settings. Saving does not deposit operating funds.

actions.label: Recognize the budget warning
actions.text: This example shows a budget warning. Saving records the settings only; add funds separately before they are needed.

actions.label: Allow devices to pick them up
actions.text: Devices apply the settings at their next check. Their operating funds remain in Network budget.

lessons.recap: Devices pick up saved settings at their next check.
